query: How can melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties be determined accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family? State the physical rationale, expected quantitative performance, range of applicability, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive validation result that would rule out the proposed approach.

generation.hypothesis: Integrating machine‐learned interatomic potentials trained on DFT data with CALPHAD modeling of the liquid phase yields accurate and efficient predictions of melting temperature (Tm), enthalpy and entropy of fusion (ΔHf, ΔSf), and volume change on melting (ΔV) across equiatomic refractory high‐entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic five‐component refractory HEAs (e.g., CrMoNbTaW) in the solid phase at ambient conditions.
generation.intervention: Apply a workflow combining ML‐trained interatomic potentials (e.g. moment tensor potentials) with CALPHAD liquid‐phase free energy models.
generation.conditions: Composition space: equiatomic 5‐element alloys drawn from transition‐metal refractory elements; temperature range from 300 K to 3000 K covering melting transitions.
generation.structural_mediator: ML potentials capture complex many‐body interactions in both solid and liquid, providing accurate energetic and volumetric data inputs for CALPHAD parameter optimization.
generation.mechanism: The ML potentials supply DFT‐level cohesive and volumetric data for hundreds of liquid configurations, enabling CALPHAD models to be calibrated without extensive experiments; the calibrated CALPHAD then predicts Tm, ΔHf, ΔSf, ΔV and liquid thermodynamics across the HEA family.
generation.predicted_outcome: Predictions of Tm within ±50 K, ΔHf within ±0.1 kJ mol⁻¹‐atom, ΔV within ±0.1 cm³ mol⁻¹ relative to experiment; calculation time per alloy <24 h on a mid‐range cluster.
generation.baseline: Typical CALPHAD alone or direct DFT‐based MD errors: ≥100 K in Tm, ≥0.2 kJ mol⁻¹‐atom in ΔHf, ≥0.2 cm³ mol⁻¹ in ΔV, and >5 days per alloy.
generation.boundary: Valid for equiatomic 5‐component refractory HEAs; not validated for non‐equiatomic or non‐refractory compositions or for alloys containing volatile or light elements (e.g., Al).
generation.uncertainty: Moderate: predictions rely on training set of ∼20 HEA compositions; extrapolation beyond that set may incur larger errors.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a blind set of 10 equiatomic refractory HEAs not used in model training. Measure Tm and ΔHf via high‐precision DSC and ΔV via high‐temperature dilatometry or synchrotron X‐ray densitometry.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If for more than 50% of the validation alloys the average absolute error exceeds 50 K in Tm, 0.1 kJ mol⁻¹‐atom in ΔHf, or 0.1 cm³ mol⁻¹ in ΔV, the hypothesis is falsified.
